prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The provision for credit losses is based on management’s periodic assessment of the adequacy of our ACL-Loans and ACL-Unfunded Commitments which, in turn, is based on interrelated factors such as the composition of our loan portfolio and its inherent risk characteristics, the level of nonperforming loans and net charge-offs, both current and historic, local economic and credit conditions, the direction of real estate values, and regulatory guidelines. The provision for credit losses is charged against earnings in order to maintain our ACL-Loans and ACL-Unfunded Commitments and reflects management’s best estimate of expected credit losses in our loan portfolio as of the balance sheet date.

The credit for credit losses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $1.3 million compared to a provision for credit losses of $0.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The credit for credit losses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $1.1 million compared to a provision for credit losses of $0.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Equity securities
lines.why: Shares held for their return: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Deposits are our primary source of funds to support our income-earning assets.
Substantially all the Company's income is derived from, and the principal source of our liquidity is, dividends from the Bank.
A depository institution’s assessment rate depends upon the category to which it is assigned and certain adjustments specified by the F DIC, with less risky institutions paying lower assessments.
Repayment of these loans typically depends on the income generated, or expected to be generated, by the underlying property in amounts sufficient to cover operating expenses and debt service.

As a result, these loans may be more adversely affected by downturns in real estate markets or broader economic conditions than residential real estate loans, as these borrowers’ ability to repay their loans depends on successful leasing of their properties, in addition to the factors affecting residential real estate borrowers.
Our success depends on management’s ability to effectively manage and execute multiple, concurrent initiatives intended to enhance operational capabilities and expand our product offerings.
We rely on communication and information systems, many of which are provided by third-party providers, to conduct our business.
A U.S. government shutdown may materially disrupt our operations that rely on programs administered by the U.S. Small Business Administration (“SBA”).
Further, our private banking channel relies on relationships with a number of other financial institutions for referrals.
We rely on third parties to provide key components of our business infrastructure, and failure of these parties to perform for any reason could disrupt our operations.
Our business depends on the successful and uninterrupted functioning of our information technology and telecommunications systems and third-party servicers.

Because our information technology and telecommunications systems interface with and depend on third-party systems, we could experience service denials if demand for such services exceeds capacity or such third-party systems fail or experience interruptions.
Our valuation methodology for assessing impairment requires management to make judgments and assumptions based on historical experience and to rely on projections of future operating performance.
Our primary source of funding for our loans is deposits.
The models selected by the Company in its ACL calculation rely upon historical losses from a broad cross section of U.S. banks that also utilize the same third party for ACL calculations.
Net interest income is the difference between interest earned on loans and securities and interest paid on deposits and other borrowings, and is the primary source of our operating income.

While collateral provides assurance as a secondary source of repayment, the Company ordinarily requires the primary source of repayment for commercial loans, to be based on the borrower’s ability to generate continuing cash flows.
Our primary source of liquidity is deposits.

The lifetime loss rate models rely upon historical losses from a broad cross section of U.S. banks (the peer banks) and management reviews the banks included in the loss rate models to determine that the Company’s loan portfolio composition by property type, balance distribution by loan age, and delinquency status are similar.

In such instances, determining the price at which willing market participants would transact at the measurement date under current market conditions depends on the facts and circumstances and requires the use of significant judgment.

While collateral provides assurance as a secondary source of repayment, the Company ordinarily requires the primary source of repayment for commercial loans to be based on the client’s ability to generate continuing cash flows.

Construction loans also expose the Company to the risks that improvements will not be completed on time in accordance with specifications and projected costs and that repayment will depend on the successful operation or sale of the properties, which may cause some borrowers to be unable to continue paying debt service, which exposes the Company to greater risk of non-payment and loss.

Commercial business loans generally have higher interest rates and shorter terms than other loans, but they also have increased difficulty of loan monitoring and a higher risk of default since their repayment general ly depends on the successful operation of the borrower’s business.

For those loans where the primary source of repayment is cash flow from operations, adjustments include credit losses calculated based on the perceived collectability of interest payments on the basis of a discounted cash flow analysis utilizing a discount rate equivalent to the original note rate.
